'''Masato Wakayama''' ({{Langx|ja|text=若山 正人|translit=Wakayama Masato}}; born November 1955) is a Japanese mathematician specializing in [[representation theory]], [[number theory]], and [[mathematical physics]]. He is the Research Principal of the NTT Institute of Fundamental Mathematics<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=NTT Institute for Fundamental Mathematics |url=https://rd-cms-prd2.gcms.gvm-jp.groupis-gn.ntt/e/ifm/ |access-date=2026-07-21 |website=NTT R&D Website |language=en}}</ref>, President of ZEN University<ref>{{Cite web |title=Message. President. Masato Wakayama |url=https://zen.ac.jp/message |access-date=2026-07-21 |website=ZEN University |language=en}}</ref> and Professor Emeritus at [[Kyushu University]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=WAKAYAMA, Masato {{!}} KYUSHU UNIVERSITY Institute of Mathematics for Industry |url=https://www.imi.kyushu-u.ac.jp/post-department/department-4809/ |access-date=2026-07-21 |language=en}}</ref>. He worked to improve research collaboration in mathematics between academia and industry and the development of mathematics among young people in Japan.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Normile |first=Dennis |date=2015-11-06 |title=Pacific Rim mathematicians coaxed from their ivory towers |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.350.6261.616 |journal=Science |language=en |volume=350 |issue=6261 |pages=616–616 |doi=10.1126/science.350.6261.616 |issn=0036-8075|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Life ==

Masato Wakayama was born in November, 1955.{{Citation needed|date=August 2026}} In 1985, he received his Doctor of Science degree in mathematics from Hiroshima University under the supervision of Kiyosato Okamoto.{{Citation needed|date=August 2026}}

He worked as an assistant professor at [[Fukuyama University]] (1986-1989) and at [[Tottori University]] (1989-1994), moving later to [[Kyushu University]], where he stayed until the end of 2019. In addition to the academic position, he held appointments as dean of the faculty of mathematics and graduate school of mathematics (2006-2010) and executive vice president of Kyushu University (2014-2019).{{Citation needed|date=August 2026}}

He led the foundation{{Vague|date=August 2026}} of the Institute of Mathematics for Industry of Kyushu University in 2011<ref>{{Cite web |title=Institute of Mathematics for Industry Inaugurated {{!}} Topics {{!}} KYUSHU UNIVERSITY |url=https://www.kyushu-u.ac.jp/en/topics/view/108/ |access-date=2026-07-21 |website=九州大学（KYUSHU UNIVERSITY） |language=en}}</ref>, a research institute dedicated to promoting mathematical collaboration between academia and industry in Japan, and held the position of founding director of the institute until 2014<ref>{{Cite web |title=Message from the Director {{!}} KYUSHU UNIVERSITY Institute of Mathematics for Industry |url=https://www.imi.kyushu-u.ac.jp/en/about/director-message/ |access-date=2026-07-21 |language=en |quote="Since its establishment, the IMI has been the first research center for industrial mathematics in Japan, thanks to the leadership of its three directors, Masato Wakayama (April 2011 – September 2014)"}}</ref>.

After concluding his period at Kyushu University, he joined [[Tokyo University of Science]] as vice president and professor at the Faculty of Science (2020-2021)<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.tus.ac.jp/sdgs/1516/ |title=[Event information – 11/17] TUS FORUM 2020 – New Initiatives for the SDGs – Looking Ahead to a Transformed Post-COVID Society –｜Tokyo University of Science x SDGs｜Tokyo University of Science |access-date=2026-07-21 |website=Tokyo University of Science x SDGs｜Tokyo University of Science |language=en|quote="After Mr. Shimada’s speech were speeches from TUS Vice President Masato Wakayama (...)"}}</ref>. Simultaneously, he occupied the position of Principal Fellow of the Center for Research and Development Strategy (CRDS)<ref>{{Cite book |title=調査報告書. 日本における数理科学とその革新：過去、現在、そして将来の展望 |date=August 2025 |publisher=Center for Research and Development Strategy, Japan Science and Technology Agency |year=2025 |isbn=978-4-88890-999-0 |pages=91 |language=ja |trans-title=RESEARCH REPORT. Mathematical Sciences and its innovation in Japan: Past, Present, and Future Prospects |quote=""若山 正人 特任フェロー" (English: Wakayama Masato. Principal Fellow"}}</ref> during 2020-2024, a public [[think tank]] of the [[Japan Science and Technology Agency]] (JST).

In 2021, he founded the NTT Institute for Fundamental Mathematics (NTT IFM) in NTT R&D<ref>{{Cite news |title=Brilliant minds sought by NTT to tackle unsolved math problems {{!}} The Asahi Shimbun: Breaking News, Japan News and Analysis |url=https://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/14476475 |archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20250722054043/https://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/14476475 |archive-date=2025-07-22 |access-date=2026-07-21 |work=The Asahi Shimbun |language=en-US}}</ref>. Belonging to the NTT Communication Science Laboratories, the Institute for Fundamental Mathematics is dedicated to basic research in mathematics with topics including algebraic geometry, number theory, representation theory, dynamical systems and graph theory<ref>{{Cite web |title=NTT has established the Institute for Fundamental MathematicsAdvancing the pace of exploration into the unexplored principles of quantum computing {{!}} Press Release {{!}} NTT |url=https://group.ntt/en/newsrelease/2021/10/01/211001a.html |access-date=2026-07-21 |website=group.ntt |language=en}}</ref>. Currently, he is the head of the institute and Fundamental Mathematics Research Principal<ref name=":0" />.

In 2025, he became the first president of ZEN University, an online university established by the Educational Institute of [[The Nippon Foundation]] and [[Dwango_(company)|DWANGO Co., Ltd]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Nippon Foundation, Dwango Open ZEN University with 3,380 Students Enrolled for Fully Online Education |url=https://tnfsa.nippon-foundation.or.jp/news/2645933 |access-date=2026-07-24 |website=TNF Scholars Association |language=en}}</ref>. Also, he has served as the president of the Mathematics Certification Institute of Japan<ref>{{Cite web |title=ごあいさつ {{!}} 公益財団法人 日本数学検定協会 |url=https://www.su-gaku.net/association/greeting/ |access-date=2026-07-21 |language=ja}}</ref>.

A conference on the occasion of his 70th birthday was held on October 2025 at Kyushu University<ref>{{Cite web |title=Quantum Interactions — from and to Number Theory, Representation Theory, and Graph Theory |url=https://imi.kyushu-u.ac.jp/~wakayama/70th/ |access-date=2026-07-21 |website=imi.kyushu-u.ac.jp}}</ref>.

He has occupied positions in institutions and committees in Japan,:

* Chair, Mathematics Innovation Committee in [[MEXT]] (2011-2017).{{Citation needed|date=August 2026}}
* Visiting professor<ref>{{Cite web |title=Faculty Profiles - WAKAYAMA MASATO |url=https://strdb.s.isct.ac.jp/html/100003878_en.html |access-date=2026-07-21 |website=strdb.s.isct.ac.jp |language=en}}</ref>, [[Institute of Science Tokyo]] (2011-present).
* Senior Advisor/Scientific Advisor<ref>{{Cite web |title=Masato Wakayama {{!}} iTHEMS |url=https://ithems.riken.jp/en/members/masato-wakayama |access-date=2026-07-21 |website=ithems.riken.jp}}</ref>, [[RIKEN]] Center for Interdisciplinary Theoretical and Mathematical Sciences (iTHEM.S) (2020-present).
* Advisor Board Member<ref>{{Cite web |title=AIMR Advisory Board {{!}} AIMR |url=https://www.wpi-aimr.tohoku.ac.jp/en/about/organization/advisory.html |access-date=2026-07-21 |website=www.wpi-aimr.tohoku.ac.jp}}</ref>, Advanced Institute for Materials Research (AIMR), [[Tohoku University]] (2025-present).
* Chair<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-06-22 |title=About｜Moonshot R&D |url=https://www.jst.go.jp/moonshot/en/about.html |access-date=2026-07-21 |website=www.jst.go.jp |language=en}}</ref>, Mathematical Science (Cross-sectional Issue in JST), Moonshot R&D Program by [[Cabinet of Japan]] (2020-present).
* Editor-in-Chief<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mathematics for Industry {{!}} Editorial board |url=https://link.springer.com/series/13254/editors |access-date=2026-07-21 |website=SpringerLink |language=en}}</ref>, Mathematics for Industry Book Series of Nature-Springer. (2010-present).   
* Editor-in-Chief<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=About APCMfI {{!}} About APCMfI {{!}} APCMFI |url=https://apcmfi.org/about/councilmembers.html |access-date=2026-07-21 |website=apcmfi.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |date=2019 |title=Editorial |url=https://www.worldscientific.com/doi/10.1142/S2661335219010019 |journal=International Journal of Mathematics for Industry |volume=11 |issue=01 |pages=1901001 |doi=10.1142/S2661335219010019 |issn=2661-3352|doi-access=free }}</ref>, International Journal of Mathematics for Industry. (2009-2025). 
* Chair and President<ref name=":1" />, Asia Pacific Consortium of Mathematics for Industry (APCMfI) (2014-2021).
* Editor-in-Chief, High School Mathematics Textbook Series "Shinpen" ({{Langx|ja|text=|新興出版社啓林館|translit=Shinko Shuppansha Keirinkan}}), (2015–2023){{Citation needed|date=August 2026}}
* Editor-in-Chief, Library of Mathematical Foundations ({{Langx|ja|text=|サイエンス社|translit=saiensu sha}}), (2017–present).

== Research ==

His contributions are mainly in the areas  of representation theory, mathematical physics, and number theory, particularly the theory of [[zeta functions]].

He stated the study of representation theory and [[invariant theory]] of the alpha-determinant, a generalization of the [[determinant]] interpolating the determinant and the [[Permanent_(mathematics)|permanent]], leading to a notion of wreath determinants for a rectangular matrix with good invariant properties. Other contributions to the theory of determinants are the extension of the [[Capelli's identity|Capelli identity]] to the context of quantum group <math>GL_q(n)</math><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Jing |first=Naihuan |last2=Liu |first2=Ming |last3=Molev |first3=Alexander |date=2025-04-04 |title=The q-Immanants and Higher Quantum Capelli Identities |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s00220-025-05273-x |journal=Communications in Mathematical Physics |language=en |volume=406 |issue=5 |pages=99 |doi=10.1007/s00220-025-05273-x |issn=1432-0916 |quote="Those coefficients were used by Noumi, Umeda and Wakayama to produce q-analogues of the classical Capelli identity."|doi-access=free }}</ref>, and a [[Pfaffian]] summation formula in terms of determinant minors for two matrices, which may be considered a Pfaffian version of the [[Cauchy-Binet formula]] for determinants<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Luque |first=Jean-Gabriel |last2=Thibon |first2=Jean-Yves |date=2002-11-01 |title=Pfaffian and Hafnian identities in shuffle algebras |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0196885802000362 |journal=Advances in Applied Mathematics |volume=29 |issue=4 |pages=640 |doi=10.1016/S0196-8858(02)00036-2 |issn=0196-8858 |quote="In [9,10], Ishikawa and Wakayama prove a minor summation formula for Pfaffians:"}}</ref>.

He also introduced the non-commutative harmonic oscillator, a matrix-valued differential operator generalizing the [[quantum harmonic oscillator]], and studied the arithmetical properties of its [[Spectral zeta function|spectral zeta functions]], obtaining relations with [[Elliptic curve|elliptic curves]], generalized [[Apéry's constant|Apéry numbers]] and [[Modular form|modular forms]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Parmeggiani |first=Alberto |date=2014-12-01 |title=Non-Commutative Harmonic Oscillators and Related Problems |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s00032-014-0220-z |journal=Milan Journal of Mathematics |language=en |volume=82 |issue=2 |pages=343–387 |doi=10.1007/s00032-014-0220-z |issn=1424-9294|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Parmeggiani |first=Alberto |date=2010 |title=Spectral Theory of Non-Commutative Harmonic Oscillators: An Introduction |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-642-11922-4 |journal=Lecture Notes in Mathematics |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-3-642-11922-4 |issn=0075-8434|url-access=subscription }}</ref>. He has also contributed to the mathematical study of the spectrum of the quantum Rabi model, a model of quantum interaction. The two models are related via a confluence process of the [[ordinary differential equation]] pictures of their eigenvalue problems.{{Citation needed|date=August 2026}}
